To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
tungsten nanoparticles can be obtained via a liquid-ammonia-mediated synthesis and that these particles are stable in the solid state and can be dispersed as a colloidal solution in alkanes.

tungsten nanoparticles were obtained in a liquid ammonia-based reaction, that they are stable in alkanes and show a grayish-orange colour due to plasmon resonance, that they show catalytic activity in hydrocarbon dehydrogenation and that they are active in CO oxidation.

(1) tungsten nanoparticles were obtained in a liquid-ammonia medium by reduction of WCl 6 with dissolved sodium, (2) the tungsten nanoparticles exhibit a diameter in the range 1-2 nm, and (3) the tungsten nanoparticle suspension in alkanes exhibits a grayish orange color, which is attributed to red-shifted surface plasmon resonance.

the synthesis of tungsten nanoparticles and the investigation of their optical and catalytic properties.

the synthesis and characterization of tungsten nanoparticles in liquid ammonia and in alkanes.
